messages:
sara: seeing a wave of coldstarts in euc3, autoscaler isn't opening new nodes fast enough, lots of pods pending :wave:

Dan: confirmed — spike started ~1796543180, pods Pending due to InsufficientGPUs and NodeCreationTimeouts :thinking_face:

ryan: autoscaler-bot shows scale decisions suppressed due to "heartbeat-mismatch" from provisioner in euc3-zone-b :eyes:

autoscaler-bot: detected: control-plane heartbeats delayed (euc3-zone-b). suppressing aggressive scale-ups to avoid overprovisioning. backoff=60s

sara: logs show the provisioner created nodes but kubelet didn't register for ~45s. attaching kubelet logs:
```
May 12 10:33:11 kubelet[1234]: Node not yet registered: kubelet failed to mount 1 block devices
May 12 10:33:56 kubelet[1234]: Registered node "ip-10-0-4-12.euc3" with 0 GPUs available
```

Dan: also seeing intermittent CNI flaps -> pods stuck in ContainerCreating. example: `FailedAttachVolume` sometimes but mostly `NetworkPlugin cni failed`

infra-oncall: jumping in — routing team, can we shift traffic to euc1/us-east1 for the next 10m while we assess? we need to reduce pressure on euc3. :ambulance:

ryan: yes, I'll mark euc3 as DRY_RUN for loadbalancer routing and nudge traffic to nearest healthy region. switching rollout policy to prefer us-east1 within 2 minutes.

sara: temp mitigation: 1) enable hotpool prewarm for critical GPU pools in euc3 (30 nodes) 2) relax autoscaler suppression for 10m 3) fallback to smaller model replicas (quantized-v2) for low-priority tenants to free GPUs. aware of cost hit for hotpool.

Dan: running the hotpool command now:
```
kubectl annotate nodepool/gpu-euc3 hotpool=prewarm --overwrite
redwoodctl nodepool scale --nodepool gpu-euc3 --replicas 30 --prewarm
```

deploy-bot: canary rollback of latest infra agent in euc3 scheduled at 10:45 if issues persist.

sara: quick check — quota for GPUs in euc3 is 120, current fault is not quota exhaustion but registration delay + CNI errors. but if we prewarm we'll hit quota; approving burst request to cloud for +40 GPUs for 1 hour. FYI costs will spike ~+$2.5k/hr.

ryan: after shifting LB weights to us-east1, error rate on model endpoints dropped 60%. still seeing delayed pod readiness in euc3 though. next step: restart CNI pods on affected nodes and drain pods sequentially to let kubelet re-register cleanly.

Dan: running CNI restart, sample commands:
```
for n in $(kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=cni -o name); do kubectl delete $n -n kube-system; done
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/aws-node -n kube-system
```

infra-oncall: monitoring dashboards — CPU/GPU utilization, node registration latency, attach volume errors all trending back down. keeping routing prefer-us-east for 20m, then reassess.

sara: open action items:
- followup postmortem (urge: include control-plane heartbeat metrics, kubelet register latency)
- add runbook step to temporarily disable autoscaler suppression if control-plane heartbeats delayed but node creation events are present
- improve prewarm playbook to auto-request short-term quota bursts
- network team to investigate CNI kubelet timing and underlying cloud attach latency

ryan: filing incident ticket and adding owners. linking runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.com/autoscaler/coldstart-wave

Dan: thanks — keeping this thread pinned. will post final TL;DR after full recovery. :white_check_mark:
